draft.name: ICU readmission after index hospital discharge
draft.sql: SELECT DISTINCT a.hadm_id FROM admissions a WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM icustays i1 WHERE i1.hadm_id = a.hadm_id AND i1.subject_id = a.subject_id) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM icustays i2 WHERE i2.subject_id = a.subject_id AND i2.hadm_id <> a.hadm_id AND i2.intime > a.dischtime)
assumptions: Index admission is the hospital admission (admissions.hadm_id) that is followed by a later ICU stay; the index admission must itself contain at least one ICU stay (icustays with the same hadm_id), since the text describes ICU readmission.
A subsequent ICU admission is an icustays row for the same subject_id with a different hadm_id whose intime is strictly after the index admission's dischtime.
Any later ICU stay in a different hospital admission counts, so multiple readmissions are covered by a single EXISTS test and each index hadm_id appears once.
Transfers back to the ICU within the same index hospitalization are excluded because they share the index hadm_id.

The clause requiring the readmission to be triggered by a newly developed or recurrent medical condition cannot be verified from the available tables without inventing a code list, so it is not applied; all subsequent ICU admissions after discharge are counted.
Admissions with a null dischtime are not matched because the comparison with intime evaluates to null.
Deaths before discharge cannot yield a readmission, which the date comparison handles without a separate rule.
